en.title: Shortest Schedule with Unlimited Parallel Development and Serial Integration
en.description:
Each feature is handled in exactly one of two ways: development takes developmentTime[i], and integration takes integrationTime[i]. Development is carried out simultaneously by as many members as needed, while integration is done sequentially by the team lead alone; the two kinds of work may overlap. Find the shortest time to finish everything. The parallel/serial conditions were recovered from the original HTML.

The input/output format was compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by two lines giving the development times and the integration times respectively. The original text gives no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, and both kinds of times are in 1..10⁹.
en.output: Output the shortest schedule length. The intermediate sum of integration times requires 64 bits.
en.explanation: The answers are 6, 3, and 1; in the second example, development and integration run in parallel, so 2 and 3 must not be added.
hints: Binary search on the schedule length T. Features whose development time is >T must be integrated, and T is feasible when the sum of their integration times is ≤T; all other features can simply be developed in parallel.
